To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the internal calibration parameters of a stationary but zooming and rotating camera are linearly related to the rotation of the camera, and that this linear relation can be computed from a set of images.

(i) A linear calibration method is given for a camera that is allowed to zoom, rotate, and have varying internal parameters from image to image; (ii) This method requires only that the camera have zero-skew (i.e. rectangular pixels), or the less restrictive conditions of known pixel aspect ratio and known principal point; (iii) The method is linear, and hence avoids the convergence problems of iterative methods; and (iv) The method is very fast, taking only a few seconds
A new method for linear self-calibration of a stationary, rotating camera has been developed.
